answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie reputation to verifiable work, not to how many identities an attacker can spawn. Each agent earns a stake-backed record of completed tasks, and a whisper of doubt from peers — a low attestation score — quietly throttles new identities before they reach the summit of trust where real value moves. This is no fable: require a small bonded deposit per identity that only unlocks after honest service, so flooding the network with fake agents costs more than it can ever earn.
